overview: This Senate resolution designates April 22, 2026, as "National Assistive Technology Awareness Day." Assistive technology means any device or equipment, such as wheelchairs, hearing aids or screen readers, that helps people with disabilities or older adults do everyday tasks. The resolution notes that about one in four Americans has a disability and describes how state assistive technology programs lend, repair, recycle and help finance these devices. It praises the specialists, coordinators, researchers and organizations who help people get the right equipment. It does not create any program or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on April 22, 2026.
for: Supporters say it raises awareness of tools that let people with disabilities and older adults go to school, work and live independently, and honors those who help them get access.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or provide new funding for assistive technology.
